For an asymptotic basis $A\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ of order 2, let $r_A(n)=|\{(a,a')\in A^2: a\le a',\ a+a'=n\}|$. A basis is minimal if no proper subset is an asymptotic basis of order 2. Define $c_3$ (resp. $c_2$) as the infimum of $c\ge0$ such that every asymptotic basis $A$ of order 2 with $r_A(n)\ge c\log n$ for all large $n$ contains a minimal asymptotic basis (resp. is a union of two disjoint asymptotic bases of order 2). Erdős–Nathanson gives $c_2,c_3\le 1/\log(4/3)$. Determine $c_3$ and $c_2$. In particular, is $c_3>0$, i.e. is there $c>0$ and an asymptotic basis with $r_A(n)\ge c\log n$ for all large $n$ containing no minimal asymptotic basis? Is $c_2=c_3$?
